lede.headline: Berkshire's cash hoard tops $377 billion as Buffett buys back stock
lede.dek: Berkshire Hathaway's operating profit fell 5.8% in the third quarter as Geico's underwriting weakened, even as the conglomerate's cash pile grew and it closed a $6.8 billion acquisition.

top10AsOf: List as of Sep 24, 2026 9:15 PM ET

stories.headline: Berkshire profit falls as cash hoard hits $377 billion
stories.move: Berkshire Hathaway's operating earnings fell 5.8% to $12.7 billion in the third quarter, as insurance underwriting profit at Geico dropped 43%. The company's cash pile rose to $377.4 billion, it bought back about $9.6 billion of its own stock, and it closed its roughly $6.8 billion all-cash acquisition of homebuilder Taylor Morrison.
stories.why: Operating profit falling even as cash keeps piling up and buybacks double shows Buffett still struggling to find places to deploy Berkshire's reserves at prices he likes.
stories.bear: A cash pile that keeps growing toward $380 billion, even after a multibillion-dollar acquisition, suggests Berkshire still sees few attractively priced opportunities.
stories.watch: Berkshire's fourth-quarter and full-year results, typically released in late February, will show whether the cash pile keeps climbing.

stories.headline: AMD posts record revenue as data-center sales nearly double
stories.move: AMD reported record third-quarter revenue of $13.38 billion, up 45% from a year earlier, beating the $13.08 billion analysts expected. Data center revenue reached $8.55 billion, nearly double a year earlier. The company guided to about $17 billion in fourth-quarter revenue, plus or minus 3%.
stories.why: The data-center number shows AMD closing the gap with Nvidia in AI chips, and the guidance signals management expects the AI buildout to keep accelerating.
stories.bear: AMD shares plunged 17% days after the report on fears that a slowdown in data-center construction, tied to the midterm election results, could crimp future demand, before partly recovering.
stories.watch: AMD's next earnings report, expected in early February, will show whether the fourth-quarter guidance holds up.

stories.headline: Airbnb posts fastest revenue growth in more than three years
stories.move: Airbnb's third-quarter revenue rose 19% to $4.87 billion, beating the $4.75 billion analysts expected, with diluted earnings of $3.16 a share against a $2.85 estimate. Gross booking value rose 21% to $27.7 billion.
stories.why: Chesky called it the company's fastest revenue growth in more than three years, a sign that cheaper listings and new booking features are pulling in more travelers.
stories.bear: Stripping out currency effects, revenue growth slows to 16%, and underlying nights-and-seats-booked growth is closer to 13% once a new pay-later feature is excluded.
stories.watch: Airbnb's next quarterly report, expected in February, will show whether booking momentum holds into the slower winter travel season.

stories.headline: Ubiquiti posts record $1 billion quarter, revenue up 40%
stories.move: Ubiquiti reported record fiscal first-quarter revenue of $1.03 billion, up 39.9% from a year earlier. Enterprise Technology revenue rose to $941.3 million from $657.1 million, and gross margin improved to 47.3% from 46.0%.
stories.why: The jump shows enterprise demand for Ubiquiti's networking gear outpacing larger rivals, even as the company flags tighter component supply as a risk ahead.
stories.bear: Management said some component costs have risen since the prior quarter and could keep climbing, which could squeeze margins and limit shipments.
stories.watch: Ubiquiti's next earnings report, expected around February, will show whether enterprise demand keeps outrunning supply constraints.

stories.headline: Arista posts record revenue, raises full-year outlook
stories.move: Arista Networks reported third-quarter revenue of $3.66 billion, up 58.5% from a year earlier, with non-GAAP earnings of $1.20 a share versus a $1.08 estimate. The company raised its full-year 2026 revenue forecast to $13.3 billion, about 48% annual growth.
stories.why: The raised outlook shows Arista's AI-driven networking demand still accelerating even as some rivals warn of slower data-center spending.
stories.bear: Despite the beat, Arista shares briefly dropped in after-hours trading, with some investors reading the outlook as short of the bigger beat-and-raise they had expected.
stories.watch: Arista's next quarterly report, expected in February, will show whether the raised full-year forecast holds.

stories.headline: Palantir's US commercial sales top government sales for first time
stories.move: Palantir's third-quarter revenue rose 95.9% to $2.31 billion. US commercial revenue jumped 148% to $984 million, overtaking US government revenue of $953 million for the first time in the company's history. The company raised its full-year 2026 revenue outlook to about $8.53 billion.
stories.why: The milestone shows Palantir, co-founded and chaired by Peter Thiel, successfully shifting from a government-contractor reputation toward winning corporate AI customers.
stories.bear: Despite the beat, Palantir's stock traded lower than before the report, as some investors questioned whether its valuation already prices in years of future growth.
stories.watch: Palantir's next earnings report, expected in February, will show whether commercial revenue keeps outpacing government work.

stories.headline: Uber bookings jump 20%, plans 700 driverless cars by year-end
stories.move: Uber's third-quarter gross bookings rose 20% to $59.8 billion, and revenue rose 10% to $14.8 billion. Adjusted EBITDA climbed 31% to $3.0 billion. CEO Dara Khosrowshahi said Uber expects about 700 fully driverless vehicles on its platform by year-end and more than 2,000 in 2027.
stories.why: The driverless-car targets show Uber racing to build out autonomous rides as a growth lever beyond its human-driven core business.
stories.bear: GAAP earnings of $0.25 a share missed Wall Street's consensus by a wide margin, and the stock fell after the report on tepid fourth-quarter guidance.
stories.watch: Watch whether Uber hits its target of about 700 driverless vehicles on its platform by the end of this year.

stories.headline: Shopify revenue jumps 32% as AI-referred orders triple
stories.move: Shopify's third-quarter revenue rose 32% to $3.74 billion, with gross merchandise volume up 29% to $119.1 billion. The company said orders arriving from AI search tools grew 3.3 times over a year earlier, from a small base it did not quantify.
stories.why: The growth shows Shopify benefiting as more shoppers find stores through AI chatbots and search tools instead of traditional search engines.
stories.bear: Revenue came in just below the $3.745 billion analysts expected, and the company guided to a lower free cash flow margin in the fourth quarter.
stories.watch: Shopify's next report, expected in February, will show whether AI-referred order growth keeps compounding from its current small base.

watch: Nov 13 — Oracle's previously disclosed layoffs of 359 Washington state employees take effect.
Nov 17 — Nvidia holds its fiscal third-quarter earnings call, covering the quarter that ended Oct. 25.
quickHits: AI infrastructure stocks sold off sharply on Nov. 5 after Democratic wins in the midterms raised fears of slower data-center spending, then partly rebounded the next day.
memo: Strong earnings didn't guarantee a calm stock reaction this week: AMD, Arista and Palantir all beat estimates and still saw sharp swings, a reminder that results and share-price moves can diverge sharply in a jittery market.

Airbnb, Uber and Shopify each leaned on a specific new feature — pay-later bookings, driverless rides, AI-referred traffic — to keep growth rates up; it's worth asking which small feature could move your own numbers.
Berkshire kept adding cash and still closed an acquisition and doubled its buyback pace — patient capital allocation and never spending for its own sake can coexist.

movers.why: Ubiquiti rose 15.3% after posting record fiscal first-quarter revenue of $1.03 billion, up 40% from a year earlier.
Airbnb rose 11.7% after third-quarter revenue grew 19% to $4.87 billion and bookings rose 21%, beating estimates.
AMD rose 11.0% as chip stocks rebounded from an election-related sell-off, helped by record quarterly revenue of $13.4 billion.
Celsius Holdings rose 7.1% after third-quarter revenue rose 17% to $847.2 million, topping analyst estimates.
